1. This is a complaint instituted under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'FSS Act') for violation of section 26 punishable under section 51 and 59(i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as FSS Act).
2. Brief facts leading to filing of the present complaint are that on 01.12.2020 at about 04:20 pm,

complainant, Naresh Kumar Sharma, the Food Safety Officer (FSO), had taken a sample of food article 'Paneer' by purchasing it, for analysis from Food Business Operator Sh. Mani Kant Jha from the premises of M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., 2nd Floor, S-20, Star City Mall, Mayur Vihar Phase-1, Delhi.
That the above said sample was lifted in presence of witness Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant.

That after inspection of the premises, FSO showed his intention of taking a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis, where the said food article was stored for the preparation of Paneer Tikka,
Chilly Paneer and Paneer Lababdar etc. for sale for human consumption, to which FBO Sh. Mani Kant Jha agreed.
That the complainant purchased a sample of approx 1 Kg of 'Paneer' from an open tray bearing no label declaration.

That the sample was taken after proper cutting and breaking into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry steel spoon and mixed properly in a clean and dry steel bowl in which it was cut and broken.

That the sample was divided into four counterparts equally immediately by putting into four clean and dry glass bottles and 20 drops of formalin was added into each sample counterpart with the help of a dropper.
That each counterpart of sample was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and Rules and Regulations made thereunder.

That the FBO's signature were obtained on the Designated Officer's slip bearing signature of the Designated Officer,
East District and wrapper of the sample counterparts in such a manner as to partly appear on the Designated Officer slip and partly on the wrapper of the samples.

That FBO also obtained signatures Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/
2 of the FBO on the labels of all counter parts of the sample.

sentences.text: The accused stated that the Paneer was bought from an FSSAI approved supplier and that they do not manufacture Paneer in the restaurant.
That after the incident, they had changed the vendor of the Paneer and that they had stopped buying Paneer form the said Vendor.
13. The accused initially stated that they would lead defence evidence but on 24.09.2025, on the submission of the accused, their evidence was closed.
The case was thereafter, fixed for final arguments.
14. I heard the submissions of both the sides and perused the record.
15. The prosecution has levelled allegation of violation of section section 3(1)(zz)(iv)(vi) and section 3(1)(zx) of FSS Act.

The sections read as under:
section 3(1)(zx) - 'sub-standard' an article of food shall be deemed to be sub-standard if it does not meet the specified standards but not so as to render the article of food unsafe xxxxx 3(1)(zz)(iv) - by the substitution of any inferior or cheaper substance whether wholly or in part; or xxxx 3(1)(zz)(vi) - by the abstraction, wholly or in part,
of any of its constituents; or

The prosecution has also alleged that the accused have violated regulation No. 2.1.16 Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 as per which the milk fat content in Paneer has been prescribed to be minimum of 50%.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the present case, the sample of Paneer was first analyzed by Food Analyst.

However, on appeal of the accused, one part of the sample was sent to RFL and vide its report dated 24.02.2021, the expert at RFL has opined that the milk fat content in the sample was less than the minimum standard prescribed i.e. 27.64 % against the minimum prescribed limit of 50%.

Since,
the report of RFL has come on record, it would supersedes the report of Food Analyst.
Reliance in this regard is placed on Andhra Pradesh Grain & Seeds Merchant Association Vs. Union of India AIR 1971 SC 246 and MCD Vs. Bishan Sarup, ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Grain & Seeds Merchant Association Vs. Union of India AIR 1971 SC 246
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: MCD Vs. Bishan Sarup, ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, in Bishan Sarup (supra) it was held that the presumption attaching to the Certificates issued by the Directorate of CFL is only in regard to what is stated in it, as to the contents of the sample actually examined by the Director and nothing more.
16.
Now, there is one interesting aspect which is of utmost importance.

As per the report of RFL,
none of the other parameters prescribed under FSS Act and Rules have been stated to have been violated which the Food Analyst has noted except the violation of regulation No. 2.1.16 i.e. shortage in milk fat content.
The sample was lifted on 01.12.2020 and examined by Food Analyst vide its report dated 08.12.2020.
Thereafter, the report was communicated by DO to FBO/accused No.1 vide letter dated 23.12.2020 and the RFL examined the sample between 12.02.2021 and 19.02.2021.

The RFL it its report dated 24.02.2021, the expert was of the opinion that the milk fat was only 27.64 % which ought to be 50% as per regulation 2.1.16 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Now, on a plain sight, it would appear that clearly, there is violation of regulation No. 2.1.16 as the milk fat content was less than 50%.

sentences.text: However, it is to be remembered that fat content gets decreased with passage of time.

Reliance in this regard is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in State Vs. Praveen Aggarwal,
Crl. Rev. P. No. 107/2012, dated 28.02.2012.

State Vs. Praveen Aggarwal,
Crl. Rev. P. No. 107/2012

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that Food Analyst in its report has categorically noted the content of milk fat which, when the sample was tested, was about 58%.
But when the sample was tested by RFL, the milk fat was reported to be around 27%.
Unlike, Food Analyst, the report of RFL has not noted any other discrepancy in the sample vis--vis the standards prescribed under the FSS Act and Rules.
There is considerable time gap between the lifting of sample and examination of sample by RFL.
There is a gap of about two months between the two dates.
If this aspect is taken into account, the accused are entitled to benefit of doubt.
As already observed above, the presumption in favour of report of RFL is not absolute and is limited to what has been stated in the report and nothing more.

Since, there is a high probability that the fat content was significantly decreased due to passage of time which when the sample was tested by Food Analyst was within the prescribed limit, the case of prosecution must fail.

17. In view of above, the accused i..e Mani Kant Jha, Rohit Dhingra and M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd. are acquitted of the charge under section section 26(1) and 26(2)(i) read with section 3(1)(zz) (iv), (vi) of the of the FSS Act, 2006, section 26(2)(ii) read with sSection 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006 punishable under section 59(i) and 51 of FSS Act, 2006.
